land.text: Li Cunxu's Jin, which he turned into the Tang: 'in spring 923, Li Cunxu declared himself emperor of Tang' at Wei Prefecture

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Established in Daming: May 923'; the Later Tang infobox lists 'Jin' among the predecessors.

land.text: 'all of Later Liang territory' (Li Cunxu entered Daliang), without Gao Jixing's Jingnan

predecessors.note: Surrender of Kaifeng 19 November 923 (Later Liang infobox).

land.text: Fengxiang Circuit, Li Maozhen's last ground, inherited by his son Li Jiyan as Tang military governor in 924
the Former Shu realm in Sichuan, surrendered to the Later Tang at the end of 925
the Later Tang realm without Sichuan and Hanzhong (Later Shu since 934); the Qin, Feng, Cheng and Jie prefectures (Xiongwu circuit) stay Later Tang land to the end

successors.note: Shi Jingtang's Later Jin took Hedong in 936 and the rest of the realm, the Xiongwu prefectures (Qin, Feng, Cheng, Jie) included, when Li Congke fell on 11 January 937 (infobox 'Overthrown by Khitan and Shi Jingtang: January 11, 937'). The Sixteen Prefectures went to the Liao under Shi Jingtang.

land.text: Sichuan with Hanzhong: the Xichuan and Dongchuan circuits under Meng Zhixiang and Shannan West, without the Qin/Feng/Cheng/Jie country

successors.note: Infobox successors: 'Later Jin; Jingnan; Later Shu'. Sichuan went to Meng Zhixiang, Emperor of Later Shu on 16 March 934; Hanzhong followed in September 934 (see ledger). The Qin/Feng/Cheng/Jie country did not pass to Later Shu from the Later Tang: the Meng Chang page has it surrender to Later Shu around the new year 947, from the Later Jin.

land.text: Gao Jixing's Jingnan, which 'would eventually, after Li Cunxu's death, effectively become independent of Later Tang'

capitals.name: Daming (Wei Prefecture, renamed Xingtang)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Daming (923)'. Coordinates are the Daming/Wei Prefecture seat used for the Tianxiong circuit in neighbouring dossiers.

capitals.name: Luoyang
capitals.note: Infobox 'Luoyang (923-936)'; 'Li Cunxu set his capital at Luoyang' (Zhuangzong page). The state ended on 11 January 937.

rulers.name: Zhuangzong (Li Cunxu)
rulers.note: Era name Tongguang ran 'May 13, 923 - June 11, 926' (Zhuangzong page); killed in an officers' rebellion in 926.

rulers.name: Li Congke
rulers.note: Infobox 934-936; the rulers table gives 934-937 (Qingtai era); overthrown 11 January 937.

correction.text: Li Cunxu's Jin plus 'all of Later Liang territory' (Kaifeng, 19 November 923); Qi (submitted 924) and the Former Shu (surrendered late 925) still outside

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Later Tang row begins only in 926, and its 923-925 years are drawn as Former Jin (922-925), Later Liang Dynasty, Qi Kingdom and Former Shu. Built as the 926 shape minus Former Shu and Qi (about 1.1 M km2 by the gazetteer's cell count, my own arithmetic; the page gives no area). 'Li Cunxu subsequently entered Daliang and claimed all of Later Liang territory.'

correction.text: the 923 realm plus Fengxiang: 'Li Cunxu allowed his son Li Jiyan to inherit Fengxiang Circuit as military governor', 'thus viewed as the end of Qi as an independent state'; the Former Shu still independent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Qi's submission in 924 (Five Dynasties page: 'in 924 Cunxu received the submission of Shaanxi's Qi kingdom'). The 926 shape minus Former Shu is about 1.2 M km2 by cell count (my arithmetic). The Qi part of Cliopatria's shape (94,436 km2) is far larger than Fengxiang alone; the qi-kingdom dossier reduces Qi to the Fengxiang country from 916.

correction.text: the full realm by the end of 925: Wang Zongbi 'forced Wang Yan to surrender the Former Shu realm to Later Tang, thus ending Former Shu'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 926 shape drawn one year early, because the Former Shu fell 'in late 925' (the campaign opened in late 925 and was over by the year's end).

correction.text: the shape unchanged but valid 926-933 only: Sichuan leaves the Later Tang with Meng Zhixiang's proclamation of 16 March 934, and the 934-936 years take the later-tang_934 keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 1,556,443 km2 (about 1.87 M by the gazetteer's cell count). The shape is the union of Cliopatria's Later Liang Dynasty, Former Jin, Qi Kingdom and Former Shu shapes (checked by intersection: it contains the whole Later Shu 936 shape and none of Jingnan's). None of the pages opened gives an area. It stays too large for 934-935, when Sichuan was Later Shu; Cliopatria's row ends in 935 although the Later Tang lasted to 11 January 937. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 926..933 from this entry's own 'valid 926-933 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the realm without Sichuan and Hanzhong: Meng Zhixiang was 'Emperor of Later Shu' from 16 March 934, and Shannan West (Hanzhong) 'surrendered to Later Shu in the last days of Meng Zhixiang's reign'; the Xiongwu prefectures (Qin, Feng, Cheng, Jie) stay Later Tang, since the Meng Chang page has them surrender to Later Shu only around the new year 947

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 934-936 (about 1.25 M km2 by the gazetteer's cell count, my arithmetic). Repaired after review: the first draft cut the whole Later Shu 936 shape, which holds 30,854 km2 of the Qin/Feng/Cheng/Jie country that the Meng Chang page dates to Later Shu only around the new year 947 ('He Chongjian ... surrendered his circuit (including Qin, Jie, and Cheng Prefectures) to Later Shu'; Shi Fengjun surrendered Feng). Shi Jingtang took Hedong in 936 (ledger) and the rest in January 937; the later-jin dossier carries 937 on.

region.text: Li Cunxu's Jin realm (Shanxi and northern Hebei) at his proclamation at Daming

ledger.note: 923: Li Cunxu proclaims the Tang at Daming. Infobox 'Established in Daming: May 923'; 'The official start of the Later Tang dynasty is in the year 923'; era name Tongguang from 13 May 923 (Zhuangzong page: 'in spring 923, Li Cunxu declared himself emperor of Tang' at Wei Prefecture). The page names the place, not a boundary; the Jin realm is the reading.

923: Li Siyuan takes Yun Prefecture, Tianping's capital, in a surprise attack. 'Li Siyuan was shortly thereafter able to capture Yun in a surprise attack' after Li Cunxu's spring 923 proclamation and before he 'entered Daliang'; the page gives no month (10 is only a sort key between the May proclamation and the November entry into Daliang) and does not locate Yun: the place is read from the name (the later-liang-dynasty dossier draws it round Tai'an).

region.text: all of Later Liang territory: 'The Later Liang controlled most of northern China'

ledger.note: 19 November 923: Li Cunxu takes Kaifeng and the Later Liang realm. Later Liang infobox 'Surrender of Kaifeng: 19 November 923'; 'Li was able to destroy the Later Liang in 923 and found Later Tang'; the Zhuangzong page: 'Li Cunxu subsequently entered Daliang and claimed all of Later Liang territory'. Jingnan is left out of the region (see the vassal pair 924-926).

923: the Later Tang capital moves from Daming to Luoyang. Infobox 'Daming (923) Luoyang (923-936)'; 'Li Cunxu set his capital at Luoyang'. The page gives no month; November is placed after the entry into Daliang that its order implies.

924: Qi submits to the Later Tang. 'After Li Maozhen's death in 924, Li Cunxu allowed his son Li Jiyan to inherit Fengxiang Circuit as military governor', 'thus viewed as the end of Qi as an independent state' (Five Dynasties page: 'in 924 Cunxu received the submission of Shaanxi's Qi kingdom').

region.text: Gao Jixing's Jingnan circuit (Prince of Nanping)

ledger.note: 924: Gao Jixing is made Prince of Nanping by the Later Tang, and Jingnan is its dependency. The Gao Jixing page: 'In 924' the Later Tang 'created him the Prince of Nanping'; infobox reign 14 April 924 (the month); after 923 he and the other Later Liang governors 'submitted petitions ... pledging loyalty' (undated). The vassal reading is mine; the jingnan dossier starts the state in 924 as independent.

region.text: the Former Shu realm in Sichuan

ledger.note: 925: the Later Tang conquers the Former Shu. Li Cunxu 'planned to conquer Former Shu and, in late 925, put his plans into action'; Wang Zongbi 'forced Wang Yan to surrender the Former Shu realm to Later Tang, thus ending Former Shu' (Five Dynasties page: 'in 925 Cunxu conquered the Former Shu'). Sichuan was the Later Tang's from the end of 925 to 934.

927: Jingnan breaks with the Later Tang. The Emperor Mingzong page: Li Siyuan 'declared a general campaign against Gao in spring 927'; the Gao Jixing page (second page) has Mingzong strip Gao of his titles in anger (undated), Gao ask again to be a Wu vassal and Wu make him Prince of Qin (after summer 928), and the campaign ended in spring 929 (the Mingzong page says Gao died in late 928, the Gao Jixing infobox 28 January 929). 927 is the page's year for the campaign, not for the end of the allegiance, so confidence 2.

region.text: Xichuan and Dongchuan under Meng Zhixiang, Prince of Shu

ledger.note: Spring 933: Meng Zhixiang is made Prince of Shu. The Meng Zhixiang page says he took command of Dongchuan after Dong Zhang's death in 932, was formally made governor of both Dongchuan and Xichuan in spring 933, and was formally created Prince of Shu in spring 933 (infobox reign as prince 933-934). Sichuan is drawn as a Later Tang dependency for a year.

region.text: Xichuan and Dongchuan under Meng Zhixiang

ledger.note: 16 March 934: Meng Zhixiang proclaims the Later Shu. The Meng Zhixiang page's infobox gives 16 March 934 for his accession as emperor of Later Shu; the Later Shu page: 'Established: 934, in Chengdu'.

union.text: Feng, Qin, Cheng and Jie Prefectures (the page names them, not their places; read as the Tianshui and Longnan country)

region.text: Sichuan: the Xichuan and Dongchuan circuits and their dependent circuits under Meng Zhixiang

ledger.note: 16 March 934: Sichuan leaves the Later Tang. Meng Zhixiang 'claiming himself to be the Emperor of Shu' (spring 934; infobox 16 March 934) after absorbing Dongchuan (932-933); the Five Dynasties page: 'In 934, Sichuan again asserted independence.'

region.text: Shannan West Circuit, headquartered at Hanzhong

ledger.note: Late 934 (September by the reign end): Hanzhong goes to the Later Shu. Shannan West Circuit, headquartered at Hanzhong, 'had surrendered to Later Shu in the last days of Meng Zhixiang's reign' (he died in autumn 934); the Meng Zhixiang page: Zhang Qianzhao (Shannan West) and Sun Hanshao (Wuding) surrendered during Li Congke's rebellion, 'allowing Later Shu to take the region south of the Qinling Mountains'.

region.text: Shi Jingtang's Hedong command round Taiyuan (about 104,000 km2 by cell count, my reading; southern Shanxi is left to the Later Tang)

ledger.note: 936: Shi Jingtang rebels from Hedong and the Khitan make him emperor of the Later Jin. The Shi Jingtang page: sent to Taiyuan as defender 'in late 932'; Li Congke moved him to Tianping 'in summer 936'; Taizong arrived in Hedong territory 'in fall 936' and 'declared Shi the emperor of a new state of Later Jin' while Jin'an was under siege (no day given); the Five Dynasties page: 'In 936, Shi Jingtang rebelled ... became emperor in this same year.' No page names the circuits that stayed Later Tang: the Hedong radius is my reading, and the rest of the realm goes in January 937.

region.text: the Later Tang realm without Sichuan and Hanzhong (Later Shu since 934); the Qin, Feng, Cheng and Jie prefectures (Xiongwu circuit) stay Later Tang land to the end

ledger.note: 11 January 937: Li Congke falls and the rest of the realm goes to Shi Jingtang. Infobox 'Overthrown by Khitan and Shi Jingtang: January 11, 937'; 'Shi Jingtang, a rebellious jiedushi, allied with the Khitan to overthrow Li Congke.' The Qin, Feng, Cheng and Jie prefectures were still Later Tang land and pass to the Later Jin with the rest (the Meng Chang page has them surrender to Later Shu only around the new year 947, from the Later Jin).

region.text: the Later Tang realm without Sichuan and Hanzhong (Later Shu since 934); the Qin, Feng, Cheng and Jie prefectures (Xiongwu circuit) stay Later Tang land to the end

ledger.note: 11 January 937: the Later Tang ends. 'Shi established the Later Jin Dynasty and ceded the strategic Sixteen Prefectures to the Liao, marking the end of the Later Tang.' The cession is Shi Jingtang's act (Five Dynasties page: he 'promised annual tribute and the Sixteen Prefectures (modern northern Hebei and Beijing) to the Khitans'); the Later Tang itself never ceded them.

wars.name: Later Tang destruction of Later Liang
wars.outcome: Li Cunxu took Kaifeng (surrender 19 November 923) and the whole Later Liang realm; the Later Liang ended.
wars.note: The Jin-Liang war that preceded it (907-923) belongs to the former-jin and later-liang-dynasty dossiers. Yun Prefecture fell to Li Siyuan in a surprise attack shortly after the spring 923 proclamation (ledger, Zhuangzong page, no month); the march on Daliang followed.

wars.name: Later Tang conquest of Former Shu
wars.outcome: Li Jiji (titular) and Guo Chongtao attacked in late 925; Wang Yan surrendered the Former Shu realm by the end of 925.

wars.name: Later Tang campaign against Jingnan

zones.text: Gao Jixing's Jingnan circuit; the Gao Jixing page has Jingnan's Gui Prefecture taken in spring 928

wars.outcome: Mingzong declared a general campaign in spring 927; Fang Zhiwen was commissioned in fall 928; Gao Jixing died (late 928 or 28 January 929) and the campaign was ended in spring 929 with Jingnan under Gao Conghui, no land changing hands permanently on the pages.
wars.note: Pages disagree on detail: the Gao Jixing page says 'In spring 928, Xifang captured Jingnan's Gui Prefecture'; the Mingzong page does not mention Gui and says Xifang Ye recaptured Kui, Zhong and Wan Prefectures, and puts the end of the campaign after Gao's death in 'late 928'. No ledger event is written because no page says the land stayed with the Later Tang.

wars.name: Later Tang campaign against Wang Du of Yiwu
wars.outcome: Wang Yanqiu besieged Ding Prefecture; the Khitan attempt to aid Wang Du failed and in early 929 his officer Ma Rangneng opened the gates; Wang Du killed himself and the Later Tang regained Yiwu.
wars.note: The page calls Yiwu 'de facto independent', not rebel, and gives no season for the start of the 928 campaign. The Wang Du page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Du_(Later_Tang)) did not load. Nominally Later Tang land throughout, so no ledger event.

wars.name: Dong Zhang's rebellion and Meng Zhixiang's independence of Sichuan
wars.outcome: Dong Zhang rebelled in fall 930 and was crushed in summer 932; Meng Zhixiang took Dongchuan, became Prince of Shu (933) and Emperor of Later Shu on 16 March 934.
wars.note: The Zhuangzong page puts a Kang Yanxiao revolt in the Shu lands in 926; the Meng Zhixiang page dates Dong Zhang's rebellion to fall 930, not 931. The Emperor Mingzong page puts the rebellion later: 'Dong and Meng rebelled in 931' (after 'late 930' preparations).

wars.name: Later Tang expedition against Xia Prefecture (Dingnan)

zones.text: Xia Prefecture, seat of the Dingnan circuit (the page gives no location; read from the name, northern Shaanxi)

wars.outcome: Li Yichao resisted Mingzong's transfer of the Dingnan command (An Congjin) and Yao Yanchou besieged Xia Prefecture in 933; the defence held, Li Yichao pled for forgiveness and the army withdrew; Dingnan thereafter showed the court no respect.
wars.note: The page gives only the year 933 and calls the defenders Dangxiang. No land changed hands: Dingnan stayed a de facto autonomous Later Tang circuit.

wars.name: Shi Jingtang's revolt against Later Tang

zones.text: the Later Tang realm without Sichuan and Hanzhong (Later Shu since 934); the Qin, Feng, Cheng and Jie prefectures (Xiongwu circuit) stay Later Tang land to the end

wars.outcome: Shi Jingtang, allied with the Khitan, overthrew Li Congke (11 January 937), founded the Later Jin and ceded the Sixteen Prefectures to the Liao.
wars.note: The later-jin dossier carries the same war and dates the proclamation to 28 November 936; neither page opened here gives a battle.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow circuits and prefectures with no surveyed lines; the Khitan frontier in the north and the Tangut and Tibetan edge in the west are the softest. No treaty fixes any Later Tang border.

notes:
Later Tang (Cliopatria 926-935, one shape). Cliopatria's row starts three years late and ends two years early: the state runs from May 923 (Daming) to 11 January 937 (infobox). The 923-925 years are drawn by Cliopatria as Former Jin 922-925, Later Liang Dynasty 911-925, Qi Kingdom 911-925 and Former Shu 911-925 (the 926 shape is exactly their union, checked by intersection); this dossier adds keyframes later-tang_923, 924 and 925 built from the 926 shape. Those four rows belong to former-jin, later-liang-dynasty, qi-kingdom and former-shu, whose dossiers carry the mirror loss and dissolve events.

Page budget: 6 pages opened in the first pass (3 shared with other states of this batch) and 4 more in the repair pass (Gao Jixing, Jingnan, Emperor Mingzong, Shi Jingtang), over the 1-2 page budget because the Later Tang page is silent on territory. The Later Tang page is nearly silent on territory: no area, no gains, no month except the January 937 overthrow. Not on any page opened: the Later Tang's relations with Wuyue, Southern Wu, Chu and the Tanguts; Lulong; the circuits that stayed Later Tang when Shi Jingtang rebelled (the Hedong radius is a reading). Repaired after review (2026-10-19): the Qin, Feng, Cheng and Jie prefectures were NOT lost to Later Shu in 934: the Meng Chang page has the Xiongwu governor He Chongjian and Feng's defender Shi Fengjun surrender them to Later Shu 'around the new year 947', from the Later Jin; they stay Later Tang to January 937 and pass to the Later Jin. Yun Prefecture is now a gain of 923 (Zhuangzong page). The Jingnan vassal pair now rests on the Gao Jixing page (Prince of Nanping 'In 924') and the Mingzong page (campaign spring 927). Wars added from the Mingzong page: Jingnan 927-929, Wang Du at Yiwu 928-929, Xia Prefecture 933; the Wang Du page did not load.

Date disagreements: the infobox gives Li Congke 934-936 and capital Luoyang to 936, the rulers table 934-937; Later Jin dossier dates the proclamation of Shi Jingtang to 28 November 936, but the Later Tang page gives only the January 937 overthrow. The Sixteen Prefectures: this dossier does not record a Later Tang loss of them to the Liao (it was Shi Jingtang's cession; the later-jin dossier has it in 938). Jingnan: the vassal pair 924-927 is a reading of 'Prince of Nanping' (confidence 2); the jingnan dossier starts the state in 924 as independent. Date disagreements: Mingzong page says Gao Jixing died in late 928, the Gao Jixing infobox 28 January 929; Mingzong page puts Dong Zhang's and Meng's rebellion in 931, the Meng Zhixiang page in fall 930.

No gazetteer names are needed beyond those that resolve; Daming/Wei Prefecture is given as coordinates.
